A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HE-SNR research. Text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, allowing reliable matching across model renaming, renumbering, and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original checkpoint evaluations, SWE-bench correlations, entropy distributions, SFT comparisons, and token-level case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds filtering ablations, threshold sensitivity, and entropy analyses across additional architectures and mathematical QA data.

M1.justification: The filtering procedure, Top-10 entropy, HE-SNR formula, high-entropy decision set, and fixed threshold remain unchanged. MoE-S/MoE-L becoming MoE-A3B/MoE-A26B discloses model identities rather than changing the proposed method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates software-engineering trajectories only. v2 Appendix E adds analysis of answer tokens from 5,000 mathematical QA samples, substantially extending domain coverage. The original SWE-bench coverage remains.

E2.justification: Figure 6 retains the same PPL, HE-PPL, and HE-SNR comparisons. LongPPL is newly discussed but not experimentally compared. Qwen2.5 and DeepSeek are additional subjects of entropy analysis, rather than competing evaluation methods.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs introduce progressive filtering controls, Kendall ranking correlation, and a threshold sweep over ln(t) for t in [2,5]. Appendix E adds Qwen2.5-72B-Base and DeepSeek-V3-Base evaluations and a four-model mathematical answer-token analysis. The original 32K/128K checkpoint protocol and SFT on over 10,000 trajectories for three epochs remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's filtered/unfiltered comparisons, v2 adds component-level filtering ablations (Table 1), threshold sensitivity (Figure 7), and tests whether entropy patterns persist across architectures and domains (Appendix E). These substantially expand the evidence testing the design choices and generality of the observed phenomenon.

E5.justification: Both versions report Pass@1 averaged over three independent evaluation runs and retain the same KDE procedure. v2 adds no repetition counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests; its added correlation results are point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds filtering correlations, threshold-response curves, and cross-model/domain entropy results. Table 1 reports raw Action versus full-pipeline Pearson/Kendall values of 0.9666/0.9440 versus 0.9649/0.9794. Appendix D also revises the 128K Step500 and Step2000 histograms: Top-1 annotations change from 97.1% to 96.8% and 94.4% to 97.1%, respectively (v1 Figure 11g,j; v2 Figure 12g,j). Original Figure 6 coefficients remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The entropy bound, Entropy-Compressed State definition, Entropy Compression Hypothesis, and Appendix C proof retain their mathematical content. The KDE derivation moves from Appendix E to F without substantive change.

C1.justification: The central HE-SNR and entropy-compression contributions remain. The introduction narrows the alignment-tax contribution from identifying 'the intrinsic source' to an empirical insight into 'an intrinsic source' in software engineering, while broadening the stated ln 3 signature from SWE capability to reasoning.

C2.justification: v2 Section 5.5 qualifies the causal interpretation of SFT-induced reasoning impairment as a potential explanation. New discussion interprets threshold stability and cross-domain entropy patterns, including the hypothesis that ln 2 reflects general reasoning while ln 3 reflects rigorous logic. Existing limitations concerning static thresholds and stylistic sensitivity remain.

D1.justification: Section 3 identifies the formerly anonymous models as LongCat-Flash-Lite, with 68B total/3B active parameters, and LongCat-Flash, with 560B total/26B active parameters. These are useful new disclosures, not evidence of changed model sizes. No code release or detailed mathematical-data provenance is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning against LongPPL, references recent SWE reinforcement-learning pipelines, and cites reports identifying the LongCat models. It removes the Textbooks Are All You Need and Orca citations. The existing compression, entropy, and alignment framing remains.

P1.justification: The introduction is locally rewritten and condensed, model terminology is standardized, and a conflict-of-interest disclosure is added. Two results subsections and Appendix E are inserted, but the overall narrative and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with filtering Table 1, the two-panel threshold Figure 7, and architecture/domain Figures 13–14. Existing figures receive model-label and correlation-notation updates. Earlier figures and case-study tables are retained with renumbering and layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The added ablation and threshold study directly strengthen support for design choices, while model identification and more cautious SFT interpretation improve transparency. Cross-domain validation remains limited to entropy distributions. Table 1 also incorrectly claims optimal performance on both metrics: full-pipeline Pearson correlation is 0.9649 versus 0.9666 for raw Action tokens. The additions provide a useful but qualified overall improvement.
